title: DPO training guide: align LLMs with human preferences
description: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) guide: align LLMs with human preferences using Soup CLI. Dataset format, YAML config, and DPO variants (ORPO, SimPO, IPO, KTO).

blocks.html:
DPO training guide: align LLMs with human preferences

Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) aligns language models with human preferences without needing a reward model — it's simpler and more stable than RLHF/PPO.

When to use DPO

  • You have a dataset of "chosen" vs "rejected" responses
  • You want to reduce hallucinations and off-topic answers
  • You want alignment without the complexity of PPO

Use DPO after SFT. A typical pipeline: Pretrain → SFT → DPO.

1. DPO dataset format

prompt, chosen and rejected may also be message lists ([{"role": "user", "content": "..."}, ...]). Since v0.76.1 every row reaches the trainer in one layout, all strings or all message lists, and a row that mixes the two in its answers is dropped at load with a reason; see Data formats.

Save as preferences.json. That one row only shows the shape of the file: Soup holds out 10% of the rows for validation by default (data.val_split), so a one-row file leaves nothing to train on. Use your real dataset.

2. Config

blocks.code:
base: ./merged                    # the SFT adapter merged into its base (see below)
task: dpo
backend: transformers             # root-level, NOT under training

data:
  train: preferences.json
  format: dpo
  max_length: 2048                # sequence length lives under data

training:
  epochs: 1
  lr: 5.0e-7                      # the key is lr, not learning_rate
  batch_size: 2
  gradient_accumulation_steps: 8
  dpo_beta: 0.1                   # the key is dpo_beta, not beta
  lora:
    r: 16                         # LoRA turns on when r > 0; there is no enabled flag
    alpha: 32

blocks.html: An SFT run saves a LoRA adapter, not a full model, and Soup does not create a latest directory. Merge the adapter into its base first and start DPO from the merged model:

Spell these two exactly. learning_rate is not the field, so it leaves you on the lr default of 2e-5 — about 40x too high for DPO, which is the difference between alignment and a wrecked model. Likewise beta is not read; the field is dpo_beta. Since v0.75.0 a misspelled key is refused when the config loads (soup train exits 1): unknown config key 'training.learning_rate' - refused. and unknown config key 'training.beta' - did you mean 'kto_beta' or 'dpo_beta'? Refused. Since v0.74.0 it was at least reported; before that it was dropped in silence, which is how a 40x learning rate reaches a real run.

Key DPO hyperparameters:

  • dpo_beta: 0.1 — KL penalty weight. Higher = stay closer to reference model.
  • lr: 5e-7 — DPO needs a much smaller LR than SFT.
  • epochs: 1 — DPO overfits quickly, rarely needs more than 1–2 epochs.

Before you train

Save the config as dpo.yaml and run soup doctor --config dpo.yaml first. Since v0.76.0 many more settings are refused when the config loads, each naming the field and what to change, so a config that loaded on an older release can stop loading. soup doctor --config prints the error and exits 2 without loading a model (it stops at the first cross-field refusal, so fix that setting and run it again until it prints no error), and since v0.77.0 it no longer prints All checks passed! above a refusal. Several things v0.76 only warned about are refused at v0.77.0, for example a staged field (validated, read by nothing) set away from its default, which stops the load with a line ending refused as of v0.77. Delete the line., and the deprecated data.remove_unused_columns: true. See Config refusals.

3. Train

In a script or CI job, pass --yes: since v0.77.0 soup train with its stdin piped or redirected and no --yes exits 3 instead of waiting at the confirmation prompt.

During training the held-out rows (10% by default, data.val_split) are evaluated at the end of each epoch and recorded as eval_loss; training.eval_steps: N evaluates every N optimizer steps instead. That is new in v0.76.0. Upstream's changelog says that through v0.75.2 no trainer on the transformers backend scheduled an evaluation, so the held-out rows were never used and val_loss stayed empty (#1223).

DPO variants in Soup CLI

Soup supports several preference-optimization methods — swap task: to change algorithm:

  • task: dpo — Direct Preference Optimization
  • task: orpo — ORPO (combines SFT + DPO in one step, no reference model)
  • task: simpo — SimPO (length-normalized, no reference model)
  • task: ipo — IPO (IPO loss, more stable than DPO on noisy data). Since v0.77.0 training.gradient_checkpointing reaches the IPO and BCO trainers, so the default false now trains them with checkpointing off, where TRL's own default (on) used to apply; set training.gradient_checkpointing: true to keep the memory you had (#797, #1778)
  • task: kto — KTO (works with unpaired binary labels). Since v0.76.0 training.batch_size must be at least 2 on every KTO run (batch_size: auto floors at 2), not only on streamed ones (#1420). Since v0.77.0 a malformed label is no longer coerced (#2126): a boolean, the strings true/false/yes/no/1/0 (case and surrounding spaces ignored) and the integers 1, 0 and -1 are read, and a null, a float such as 1.0 or any other value drops the row at load with a reason (KTO label must be a bool, true/false string or -1/0/1 integer, got: None). soup data validate --format kto lists the reasons for the first rows it drops and still exits 0 while any row is valid; add --min-valid-fraction 1.0 to stop on one bad row

On Apple Silicon, backend: mlx trains dpo, orpo, simpo and kto natively since v0.77.0 (task: preference is still refused there); each MLX preference task refuses its own list of settings at load, so see MLX backend.

SimPO has one more check. Through v0.75.2, on trl 0.29, a row whose chosen outgrows data.max_length lost its whole rejected, the length-normalised log-probability became 0/0, every LoRA tensor went NaN and the logged loss read 0.0. Since v0.76.0 task: simpo refuses such a dataset before the first step, naming how many rows are affected and the data.max_length involved (#1208). If you trained SimPO on an earlier version with long chosen answers, check the adapter. Since v0.77.0 task: simpo on the transformers backend also caps the prompt as DPO and ORPO do (#2112, #2116): after trl tokenizes a row, the prompt is cut to data.max_length // 2 tokens, keeping its end, and the answers to the room left, so no sequence exceeds data.max_length; through v0.76.1 a long prompt reached the model whole. A prompt longer than data.max_length // 2 tokens is cut even when the whole row would fit, until upstream's #1196 lands (#1185).

Schedules, blends and streaming

  • training.dpo_beta_schedule is wired from v0.76.0 and needs dpo_beta_end. Through v0.75.2 a run that set it on dpo, ipo or preference stopped at step 0, because the callback was not a Hugging Face TrainerCallback (#1229, #1294); there is no finished run to re-check. training.dpo_ref_regen_epochs is wired under LoRA (#1345, #1636): it copies the active adapter into the frozen ref adapter every Nth epoch, and it is refused with lora.r: 0. Through v0.75.2 a run that set it on dpo, ipo or preference stopped when training started, for the same reason. This config loads:

blocks.code:
training:
  dpo_beta: 0.1
  dpo_beta_schedule: linear
  dpo_beta_end: 0.05          # required with dpo_beta_schedule
  dpo_ref_regen_epochs: 2     # every 2 epochs; needs lora.r >= 1

blocks.html:
• task: preference with preference_loss_weights blends DPO, IPO, SimPO and ORPO terms in one run. Since v0.77.0 a dpo or ipo term trains under any primary (#1785, #1828), and the reference runs once more per step; with a simpo or orpo primary, init_strategy: pissa, olora or loftq (or use_olora) is refused at trainer setup before the model loads, and under lora.r: 0 such a term still stops at the first step; relora_steps beside a blend that names dpo, ipo or bco is refused at config load, and a blend that mixes bco with a paired loss is still refused at trainer setup. (Since closed in v0.77.0: on v0.76.0 and v0.76.1 a blend naming dpo or ipo stopped at the first step.) See Preference Variety for the details and the re-run rows.
  • Resumed runs. Through v0.76.1 soup train --resume on task: dpo or ipo (and task: preference with dpo or ipo) "restored the optimizer and the step counter and trained a freshly initialised adapter" (#1768, #1797). Upstream: "Re-run any dpo, ipo or grpo training that was resumed from a checkpoint."
  • ReLoRA. training.relora_steps is refused at load since v0.77.0 on dpo, ipo, kto and bco (and a preference run whose loss or blend names dpo, ipo or bco): every ReLoRA restart merged the trained adapter into the base weights trl reads the reference from, so on v0.76.0 and v0.76.1 "from the first restart on the reference was the policy as of that step, without an error" (#1835, #1891). Remove relora_steps and train again.
  • DPO also runs over a layer-streamed base (training.stream_layers: true). On an untied checkpoint such as Llama-3.1-8B, dpo and kto failed at the first backward through v0.75.2 and hold a private copy of the output head per step from v0.76.0; see Streaming preference losses. That page also explains why the memory pre-flight refuses a Llama-3.1-8B preference run on a 4 GB card.
